newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan Taleban make their presence known in north.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban make their presence known in north.

text.p: Islamic Taleban fighters with black beards and turbans patrolled the northern Afghan city of Mazar-i-Sharif on Monday, establishing a highly visible presence in the former opposition stronghold.

Taleban troops armed with rocket-propelled grenades and rifles roamed the northern capital, captured from the ethnic Uzbek leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum on Saturday by his former second-in-command General Abdul Malik.
The city was calm, but a few distant explosions could be heard. The source of the explosions was not immediately known.
Civilian men walked or cycled through the streets, gaping curiously at the 2,500 Taleban fighters who swept into the city on Sunday night.
Few private cars were visible and mule-drawn carts provided the only form of public transport.
The airport has not reopened since Saturday's takeover of the city. Foreign aid workers were keeping a low profile, staying in their homes and offices for the time being.
"We have had no security incidents since Taleban arrived," one aid worker said, adding that Malik's forces had recovered two of three vehicles stolen in the chaos when the city fell.

Malik, who joined forces with the Taleban after staging his anti-Dostum mutiny a week ago, announced that Islamic Sharia law would be applied in the north, saying girls and women would be excluded from schools and universities until there was enough money to build segregated facilities.

Very few women were to be seen on the streets on Monday and a few who ventured out were wearing burqa, the all-enveloping Islamic veil with gauzed mesh for the eyes. "I am not too worried about the Taleban now," said one taxi driver. "But when they get full control of the city, we may have problems playing music in the car."
The Taleban have banned music cassettes in other parts of Afghanistan under their control, in conformity with their rigidly fundamentalist interpretation of Islam.
